title: venue-selection-customer-constraints-jam-session
content:
Jam session notes: venue selection & customer constraints (raw, working)

Purpose
- Quick reference notebook for SEs when sizing a deployment recommendation during discovery calls and whiteboards.
- Emphasis: pragmatic heuristics to choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and a lightweight POC path for each.

Context
- Workshop run 2025-01-28 with product, solutions, and an SRE rep to capture common variations we keep revisiting in presales.
- Observed repeated friction: customers latch on to "private because compliance" without exploring hybrid fallbacks; ops cost surprises for blunt reserved capacity estimates.

Top-level heuristics (one-line summaries)
- Hosted: recommend when latency requirement >100ms is acceptable, data residency ok with hosted regions, rapid time-to-value prioritized, and cost sensitivity moderate.
- Dedicated: recommend when predictable throughput is needed (steady high qps), customers want reserved capacity to avoid cold starts, or require SLA-backed uptime.
- Private: recommend only when strict data sovereignty, network isolation, or audited on-prem controls are non-negotiable. Also for intermittent-connectivity edge use-cases.

Decision matrix (notes, not a formal table):
- Data sensitivity: if PHI/regulated and cannot leave VPC/HSM -> Private. If contractual NDA but allowed in a contracted cloud region -> Dedicated with encrypted storage.
- Latency: sub-50ms p50 near-user -> private edge or colocated dedicated (regional). 50-150ms -> Dedicated in same region. >150ms -> Hosted is acceptable.
- Throughput volatility: bursts 10x baseline -> Hosted with burst pool OR Dedicated with burst config; if burst exceeds committed capacity regularly, propose hybrid (Dedicated + Hosted overflow routing).
- Cost predictability: if customer requires stable unit costs and monthly budgeting -> Dedicated reserved -> commit model. If pay-as-you-go preferred -> Hosted.
- Integration complexity: if network peering/VPC endpoints allowed -> Private or Dedicated; if not -> Hosted.

POC playpaths (minimal friction to outcome)
1) Hosted-first fast POC (2–7 days)
   - Goal: validate UX and inference quality end-to-end with real payloads.
   - Steps: seed API keys -> deploy sample routes -> run 10k calls/day for 3 days -> capture latency/cost/quality traces.
   - Success signals: acceptable latency p95 per SLA, cost per session estimate less than threshold, model quality passes evaluation prompts.
   - Risks: production scale differences, network egress for customer data flows.

2) Dedicated smoke POC (2–3 weeks)
   - Goal: validate throughput and steady-state latency, autoscaling behavior under sustained load.
   - Steps: size initial GPU units based on token/sec heuristics -> reserve trial capacity -> run synthetic traffic that mirrors expected qps and sequence length -> observe autoscale/fallback behavior.
   - Success signals: ability to sustain target qps with headroom, predictable cost projection for commit levels.
   - Notes: include a fallback routing plan to Hosted for overflow during trial so we can observe circuit-breaker behavior.

3) Private bridge POC (3–6 weeks)
   - Goal: validate network setup, keys, audit logs, and occasional on-prem inference runs.
   - Steps: agree on network diagram -> small on-prem VM or private k8s cluster -> deploy private control-plane stub -> run end-to-end encrypted calls -> collect audit logs.
   - Success signals: KMS integration works, audit trails match retention policy, ops runbook for patching and upgrades viable.
   - Common blockers: security policy approvals, customer change freeze windows.

Conversation checklist for discovery (questions to ask)
- Who owns the data classification? Are there contracts that prohibit cloud providers or third-party data processing?
- Expected p95 latency target and typical/90th sequence length.
- Forecasted concurrent users and peak qps per minute/hour/day for first 6 months.
- Acceptable time-to-value for an initial POC (days vs weeks) and decision gate criteria.
- Any existing infra we must integrate with (VPC peering, SIEM, Okta/SSO, KMS/HSM)?
- Are there geographic residency requirements? Specific cloud regions mandated?
- Budget model preference: committed monthly vs pay-as-you-go? Headroom multiplier allowed for peak?

Sizing heuristics (very rough quick math for initial sizing)
- If median seq len < 128 tokens and target throughput < 100 rps -> 1 GPU (A100y style) Dedicated would be borderline; Hosted may be cheaper.
- For long sequences (>512 tokens) multiply token/sec by 3x for GPU latency headroom.
- If expected sustained qps > 300 -> start talk about Dedicated pool; if <50 -> Hosted likely fine.
- Add 20–30% headroom for KV cache miss patterns and safety bursts.

Operational notes and runbook snippets (practical obs from SRE)
- Circuit-breaker policy: default route to hosted fallback when dedicated utilization > 85% for 30s.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 24 hours, metric checks on p50/p95, error rate, and unit cost delta.
- Observability: require token-level sampling for first 72 hours of POC to assess prompt-level cost.

Unresolved/decision items we should formalize into templates
- Standardized cost comparison spreadsheet template that shows Hosted vs Dedicated commit tiers vs Private fixed runbook costs for 12 months.
- A clear checklist for legal for "allowed processing" that sales can use in calls.
- Automation for a hybrid overflow demo (traffic splitter + synthetic bursts) to show in customer-facing demos.

Risk register (high level)
- Security approval delays (mitigation: pre-clear common patterns with legal/compliance).
- Customer underestimates burst patterns (mitigation: always run a short burst test during POC and show cost delta).
- Onboarding time for private > expected (mitigation: ship a "private quickstart" with minimal network requirements).

Action items
- Aisha: create a starter cost-comparison sheet and drop in SE templates folder (due 2025-02-06). Linked artifact: GH PR for template.
- Marco: prototype hybrid overflow demo wiring to hosted fallback (prototype by 2025-02-14).
- Sofia: draft Legal quick checklist and standard phrasing for "processing allowed" to hand to AE (due 2025-02-10).

Snippets for slide deck (for customer-facing summary)
- Slide: "Decision lens" with 4 callouts: Data Residency, Latency, Throughput, Cost Profile.
- Slide: "POC Paths" concise bullets: Hosted (fast), Dedicated (predictable), Private (isolated).
- Slide: "Next steps" A/B test candidate workloads -> choose POC path -> run 2-week validation -> decision review.

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Keep examples anchored to concrete numbers (qps, seq len) — customers remember those better than fuzzy adjectives.
- Avoid over-committing on private timelines during first call; set expectation for legal/security gating.

End of jam session notes. Keep this doc as a living checklist; update after next presales debrief.
